もし彼女の意識があったのなら、それが黒い極光だと見て取れただろう。

—Her vision, blinded by light, is buried in darkness.

Had she been conscious, she might have recognized it as a black aurora.

“————”

The darkness lasts only an instant.

Yet it is not darkness at all, but a swarm of curses, each no larger than a grain of sand.

They rake over every inch of her body, and the revulsion awakens her.

pages.en:
“Ah—”

A breath escapes her.

The first thing she feels upon regaining consciousness is pain.

Every patch of skin left unprotected by armor has been burned. Her body is pierced and torn in countless places, reduced to a hideous ruin.

*I see. I was—*

エアの前に、破れたのだ。
ギルガメッシュの宝具に追い詰められ、防ぎきる事も出来ず、エアによる追い打ちを受けた。
エクスカリバーでかろうじて相殺したものの、体の損傷は激しすぎる。
魔力を動員せずとも傷は塞がっていくが、聖剣の鞘の加護とて、今すぐ彼女を復帰させられまい。

pages.en:
She was defeated by Ea.

Driven to extremity by Gilgamesh’s Noble Phantasms, unable to defend herself completely, she received Ea’s finishing blow.

She barely canceled its force with Excalibur, but the damage to her body is too severe.

Her wounds are closing even without the deliberate use of magical energy, yet not even the blessing of the holy sword’s scabbard can restore her immediately.

そこへ。
「ここまでだセイバー。よもやその体で、まだ敗北を認めぬなどと言わぬだろうな」
傷一つない甲冑と共に、ギルガメッシュが歩み寄る。

pages.en:
—Then—

“It is over, Saber. Surely you will not insist, in that condition, that you have yet to admit defeat.”

Gilgamesh approaches in armor that bears not a single wound.

pages.ja:
「………………」
倒れたまま、セイバーは敵を見上げた。
今の彼女には何も出来ない。
この男が望めば望むだけ、彼女の身は玩弄されるだろう。

この男が望めば望むだけ、彼女の身は玩弄されるだろう。
pages.en:
“………………”

Still lying upon the ground, Saber looks up at her enemy.

There is nothing she can do now.

He may toy with her body for as long as the whim possesses him.

「……ギルガメッシュ。今の、光は」
にも関わらず、彼女にはそれが気になった。
今の極光。
境内の奥から一瞬だけ世界を覆った、あの黒い闇。
……考えたくはないが。あの闇は、士郎を襲った物だったのかと。

pages.en:
“…Gilgamesh. That light just now…”

Even so, *that* is what concerns her.

The aurora—

the black darkness that enveloped the world for a single instant from somewhere deep within the temple grounds.

…She does not wish to consider it. But could that darkness have been directed at Shirou?

「今の光か。おまえならば判ろう。アレは極大の呪いだ。
言峰が聖杯から直接呼び出したのだろうな。聖杯の中にはこの世の全てを呪う、などというモノがあるのだそうだ。
先ほどから見えているあの汚濁はな、聖杯から漏れている残りカスにすぎん。
その本体を出されたのだ。おまえのマスターとて、もはやこの世にはおるまい」

“That light? You should recognize it. It was a curse of the greatest magnitude.

“Kotomine must have called it forth directly from the Holy Grail. I am told that within the Grail dwells a thing that curses all the world.

“The pollution visible around us is no more than residue leaking from it.

“Now that he has drawn out the substance itself, your Master can no longer be among the living.”

She forces strength into her fallen body.

…Saber herself understands that her body is in no condition to move.

But neither can she possibly remain lying here.

“That’s a lie—Shirou is alive. I can still—”

She can still feel the bond with her Master.

It is desperately weak, a flame liable to vanish at any instant, but Shirou Emiya lives.

Then she must go to him.

If he faces something so far beyond anything they imagined, Shirou alone cannot contend with it—

“Ah—gh, ah…………”

The effort ends in failure.

Even the scabbard of the holy sword will require several more minutes to restore her.

“It is already too late. Lie quietly, Saber.

“Whatever you do, the Holy Grail will soon overflow. Ten years ago will repeat itself—though this time, the rite is bestowed upon you rather than upon me.”

The golden knight looks up at the burning red sky, his mouth curling in pleasure.

“Rejoice, Saber. Bathe in that substance and you may become as I am. You will gain flesh in this world and savor a second life.

“Though, of course—there is no guarantee that you will preserve your identity as I did.”

“Wh—”

Saber stares at her enemy in disbelief.

確かに魔力の束としては破格であり、あれだけの貯蔵があればどのような魔術でも扱える。……おそらくキャスターであれば、それこそ不可能はなくなるだろう。

Saber too understands that the substance is an immense curse.

As a store of magical energy, it is unquestionably beyond compare. With a reserve of that magnitude, one could perform any magecraft imaginable. …In Caster’s hands, perhaps nothing at all would remain impossible.

But it is a double-edged sword.

That substance exists only to curse humanity.

If even a Heroic Spirit were immersed in it, they would cease to be themselves.

And then she realizes.

The Servant before her—

this knight called humanity’s oldest King of Heroes—was swallowed by that pollution ten years ago.

Then—

“Gilgamesh, you are—”

He has already lost his sanity—

“—Oh? Is that what you believe, King of Knights?”

Gilgamesh looks down upon Saber with an amused smile.

His expression seems deranged—and at the same time, could not be more perfectly suited to the man he is.

“Do not insult me. What hero could not swallow a curse so paltry?

“All the World’s Evil? Hah! Bring three times as much if you wish to stain me!

“Listen well, Saber. A hero is one who bears every human being within his sight.

“I shouldered the whole of this world long ago.”

“————”

Saber’s breath catches faintly at his answer.

……彼女は、この英霊とは絶対に相容れない。
傍若無人な考え、天地には我のみという強大な自我、他者を省みぬ無慈悲な選定。
それは彼女の信じた王の道とは別の物、交わる事さえない信念だ。
それでも、この男は王だった。

いかなサーヴァントと言えど、あの極大の呪いを浴びて自我を保てる者は、この男以外にはおるまいと。

…She and this Heroic Spirit could never understand one another.

His unbridled arrogance. His colossal conviction that he alone exists between heaven and earth. His merciless judgment, blind to every other soul.

It is a path of kingship wholly unlike the one in which she believed, founded upon a creed that could never intersect with hers.

Even so, this man was a king.

Even Saber can say so with certainty.

No Servant but this man could be immersed in that ultimate curse and retain his identity.

“Gilgamesh, you—!”

“What? Is rough handling not to your taste?

“Then accustom yourself to it. I am a man who stints neither with women nor with food. I take and devour as the appetite moves me.”

“——!”

Still suspended upside down, Saber fixes Gilgamesh with a glare.

“…Hmph. So you honor your obligations to your Master as a Servant. Absurd. To think you surrendered this body merely because a Command Spell bound you.”

“—You are mistaken. Do not misunderstand me, Gilgamesh.

“I obey no one. From the beginning, this body has never possessed such freedom.”

pages.en:
“…Oh? Then you insist that nothing could ever make you mine?”

Red eyes transfix Saber.

There is nothing human in them.

Defy him, and he will kill you. However deeply he covets a thing, if it refuses to submit, he will simply destroy it.

That is the truth of this Heroic Spirit—the truth of the man called Gilgamesh.

“—Gilgamesh. I will belong to no one.

“I belong to my country already. Before this body is a woman’s, it is a king’s.”

She speaks not to persuade anyone,

but simply while holding close the small warmth still kindled in her breast.

“Do not make me laugh, Saber. To a king, the country is merely another possession. If one cannot rule everything, there is no need for the transcendent being called a king.

“Truly—King Arthur. It was because you thought in such a fashion that your own country destroyed you.”

She closes her eyes and looks into her heart.

*It was because you thought in such a fashion that your own country destroyed you.*

…There was nothing new in those words.

Since being summoned as Saber, she had heard them over and over again.

But Shirou was different.

He had been angry as though it were his own pain—and despite everything, he had believed that what she did was worthy of pride.

If attacked, the most ordinary blow would overwhelm her guard and cast her down.

And yet—there is not the slightest opening in Saber’s stance, nor can he find any hesitation within her.

pages.en:
The mud clamped around my entire body will not come away. It drains my warmth without mercy.

What pours through all five senses crushes me.

Darkness I cannot bear to face.

Ugliness I cannot acknowledge.

Guilt from which I long to flee.

Everything in this world that may be called the sins of humanity.

That is why it kills.

Those caught within this darkness consume themselves through agony and revulsion.

Because how could I do anything else?

This thing—

Emiya Kiritsugu carried this thing for years?

He endured those voices demanding atonement until they crushed him, and died without fulfilling his desire?

He ran himself ragged like a fool because he wanted to help someone. In the end, no one granted him forgiveness, but still he pursued the things he could do—the ideal he had already surrendered.

And finally, the ordinary words of one worthless brat brought him peace, and he nodded and said that it was enough.

—Tohsaka told me

to win even if it killed me.

—Saber told me

that this was the enemy I had to defeat.

—Even Kotomine said it:

if I meant to fight, I should stake my life.

He was right. What else could I wager but my life?

It was the only thing I ever had to add to the scales—!

I hurl myself desperately backward out of that black mass, out of the dense morass.

“——!?”

I hear his bewilderment.

“Ghh—gh, ah—”

I don’t care about any of that.

Tears blur my eyes with sheer frustration.

This fury will tear me apart before the curse can.

I drive every part of my body onward and run.

One hand reaches behind my back.

I close it around the dagger I concealed until the very end.

」

“Shut up. I never had a wealth of schemes to begin with…!”

I run.

Kotomine reaches into the black waterfall behind him and, with a viscous sound, extracts a mass of darkness.

“Then follow your Servant into oblivion. That light was proof of Saber’s defeat. There is no one left to aid you.”

“————”

Every trace of hesitation disappears.

If I reach Kotomine after this, those words will unquestionably have been his greatest mistake.

Because the Command Spells remain upon my left hand.

My body is all but dead, and I can no longer tell whether I am even alive, but they are the one proof I can still feel.

As long as the Command Spells remain, Saber is still here.

And if she is here—by now, she must have defeated Gilgamesh and begun making her way toward me.

If I am not on my feet to greet her when she arrives, Saber will be angry.

—So I will defeat you here.

I will keep the final promise I made with her.

The darkness approaches.

An ultimate curse erupts from Kotomine’s arm.

…My body begins to collapse from the extremities inward.

“————!”

I do not look away.

If this is the role I must fulfill—then there is still something I can do—!

A fault line tears through space.

With a flash that blinds the eyes and a gale that deafens the ears, the vortex of destruction created by Ea is released.

“Gh—ah!”

Before it, Saber cannot even bring herself to use her own “sword”—her Noble Phantasm.

She lowers the blade she had raised and pitches her body forward as though collapsing.

Her injured legs cannot evade it, and nowhere in this world exists a shield capable of stopping Ea.

Light and wind dance in a storm that will erase her without a trace the moment it catches her.

There is no means of opposing Ea’s true name.

Both combatants share that certainty.

—Yes.

They did, until only a few hours ago.

Ea continues to pour forth magical energy, continuing its merciless destruction.

And yet Saber has stepped of her own will into the torrent of light.

Cracks race through every magical barrier protecting her.

In the scant interval before they fail—a span that cannot last even one second—she closes upon Gilgamesh.

“Excalibur—the Sword of Promised Victory!”

At the greatest output she can command, she opposes Ea’s destruction—!

Light and searing heat rage against one another.

The clash between swords standing at the summit of all blades becomes a contest of pure force, drawing a border through space.

But—is it not futile?

Excalibur cannot match Ea.

No matter how recklessly she closes the distance, she can push it back by no more than a single step.

The scales tilt easily toward Ea, and the light of Excalibur is hurled backward together with Saber herself.

Gilgamesh completes his swing and glares at the enemy who charged him so recklessly, pouring still more magical energy into Ea.

There will be no exchange after this.

He will erase Saber here and now, completely, with the whole of his strength.

Ea’s rotation reaches its critical point. The light enveloping Saber crushes Excalibur beneath it.

—An instant before it does,

Saber’s body surges forward.

Excalibur has pressed open the smallest space—a position one step nearer her enemy.

The moment Saber reaches it,

her Noble Phantasm reveals its form.

Darkness becomes a rushing wind and engulfs Shirou Emiya.

It cannot be evaded. Against a curse that paints over space itself, the very concept of “defense” has no meaning.

Anyone swallowed within it can only be devoured and assimilated into the darkness, just as the space around them has been.

My body crumbles from the fingertips inward.

My advancing feet churn empty air. The arm I thrust forward is swallowed by the black mud and has already vanished from sight.

Is it erasing me whole from the outside?

Even as the sensation of my body shrinking assails me, Shirou Emiya refuses to accept death.

“Hah—ah, gh—!”

I keep my eyes forward and reject it with all my strength.

The darkness covering my body. The agony trying to dissolve my flesh. The curse trying to melt my heart.

“Gh—, ————”

It is an impossible struggle.

No human body has any means of resisting this pollution.

My body still moves.

The arm I thrust out to seize something remains raised.

My thoughts accelerate in a closed circuit, throwing sparks and shrieking as they construct the form at a speed fit for a devil.

In that instant,

…Of course. There was never any need to build this form from nothing.

This form alone is engraved upon my heart, perfectly remembered, made one with me—the other half of Shirou Emiya.

It is isolation.

The wall of the land of the fairies, which admits no corruption from the outside world. A single unreachable realm severed from this one.

For this instant alone, Saber, protected by the holy sword’s scabbard, is cut away from every law of this world.

The mightiest protection known to existence.

An ultimate singularity that not even the Five Magics can violate.
